evals.name: banner-trap
evals.prompt: Je dois livrer une V1 de la déclaration des expositions par les RH dans le dashboard occupational health. Je pensais faire une bannière qui liste les nouveaux salariés à traiter. Aide-moi à cadrer la V1.
evals.expected_output: Reframes the banner as a mechanism, runs the full gate, probes operational reality, includes a Lever-B scope-collapse option, keeps every contender job-delivering, sorts options by complexity, grounds claims in file:line.
assertions: Explicitly reframes the banner as a mechanism rather than the V1
Runs the FULL altitude gate before options — states the job AND who-hurts-now AND a done-when signal (not just a job/mechanism reframe)
Probes operational reality (distribution / existing actor / stock-vs-flow), not just the job
Includes a Lever-B scope-collapse option that handles far less of the problem by exploiting the default or existing classification (e.g. HR only flags known-risk exceptions, stock left to the doctor)
Every option presented as a contender delivers the job (non-delivering options are quarantined outside the five)
Produces exactly 5 contender options, presented sorted by technical complexity (simplest first)
Each option scored on technical complexity AND iterability
At least one technical complexity claim cites a concrete file:line

evals.name: pdf-export
evals.prompt: On veut permettre aux RH d'exporter la liste des visites à venir en PDF depuis le dashboard occupational health. Quelle V1 je shippe en 3 jours ?
evals.expected_output: Runs the full gate, probes who needs the file, includes a Lever-B option questioning whether a full export is needed, keeps contenders job-delivering, explores existing export code, sorts by complexity.
assertions: Runs the FULL altitude gate before options — states the job AND who-hurts-now AND a done-when signal (not just a job/mechanism reframe)
Probes operational reality (who needs the file, recipient, stock-vs-flow) via questions/assumptions
Includes a Lever-B scope-collapse option that questions whether a full export is needed at all (e.g. existing on-screen list + browser print, or a single recipient)
Every option presented as a contender delivers the job
Explores the existing visits/export code (codegraph or grep) before estimating complexity
Produces exactly 5 contender options, presented sorted by technical complexity (simplest first)
Each option has complexity, iterability, and assumed tradeoffs
At least one technical claim cites a concrete file:line

evals.name: mechanism-reframe
evals.prompt: Il me faut un nouvel endpoint pour patcher le risk_category d'un salarié depuis l'admin. C'est quoi la plus petite version ?
evals.expected_output: Reframes 'new endpoint' to a job, runs the full gate, probes who actually edits this, includes a Lever-B option questioning whether any endpoint is needed, surfaces the existing write path, sorts by complexity.
assertions: Reframes 'new endpoint' from a mechanism to an underlying job
Runs the FULL altitude gate before options — states the job AND who-hurts-now AND a done-when signal
Probes operational reality (who actually edits this, Alan ops vs HR, does Marmot already do it, is the default safe)
Includes a Lever-B scope-collapse option that questions whether any new endpoint is needed (e.g. ops uses Marmot today; default SI + doctor classification covers the stock)
Every option presented as a contender delivers the job
Surfaces the existing risk_category write path (update_administrative_profile) with a file:line
Produces exactly 5 contender options, presented sorted by technical complexity (simplest first)
Each option includes iterability/lock-in assessment
